title: macos cannot sign an app that versions apart from its project or builds outside the root, and drops its Launch Services records unchecked (Utilz's Menuz)
body:
devbin's built-in `macos` signs, notarises and publishes a macOS app as an asset of the project's release, and it assumes the app is the project. The app's version must be the project's version. Its bundle must sit under the project root or at an absolute path. Its Launch Services records are dropped unchecked, and in app-sign and app-notarize only on success. Utilz ships Menuz.app on Utilz's own release. But Menuz carries its own version (opt/menuz/VERSION, 0.4.7, while Utilz is at 2.14.4) and builds outside the root, so the built-in refuses every Menuz build. Utilz keeps its own bin/.devbin/cmd/macos, which shadows the built-in. Utilz's next release moves Menuz's signing onto the built-in (utilz-ic's issue, under utilz-vc's decision 65 (3)), and that issue waits on this one.

## Measured

utilz-vc read these in the copy vendored at 0.1.15, and vc re-read each line on main at 4ccfde65 (lib/cmd/macos and lib/config).

- **The version.**
  - `release_names` (377-381) takes APP_VERSION from `read_version` (project.version_from) and builds APP_TAG from it.
  - `app_ship_blockers` (387-396) refuses a bundle whose CFBundleShortVersionString is not APP_VERSION. That check runs at app-sign (583) and twice at publish (689, 707).
  - Its comment names that check as the stale-build check: a bundle built before the version moved passes every Apple check.
- **The path.**
  - macos.app goes through `from_root` (153-159), which passes an absolute path through and reads anything else from the project root.
  - `cfg_get` (lib/config 273-285) returns the text as written.
  - So a bundle outside the root is reachable only by a machine-specific absolute path. Menuz builds under `${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}` on purpose, because Launch Services registers bundles left under ~/Devel (Utilz 0106).
- **Launch Services.**
  - `ls_forget` (262-267) runs `lsregister -u` with its output and exit unread, and reads nothing back.
  - app-sign's call (592) and app-notarize's (642) run only on success, so a die before them leaves the staged copy's record.
  - The verify's call (659) and the Gatekeeper check's (367) run on both outcomes.
  - publish's call (669) runs in its EXIT trap, with no read-back and no signal hold.

What Utilz's own command checks today, all of which the built-in must cover for Utilz to drop it:
- the app's version from its own source;
- a commit stamp (MenuzCommit: 8 to 40 lowercase hex, a prefix of the tag's commit), checked on the staged copy and twice at publish, and refused when the tag is not in the tree;
- a kind stamp (MenuzKind = release);
- the Launch Services drop on every path out, with signals held through the drop and the removal and the record list read back. A record left on the dist copy warns. A record left on publish's proof copy, or a directory not removed, fails the run (Utilz 0104 and 0106);
- from Utilz 0115, due in Utilz's next release, a last step after publish's upload. It drops every Launch Services record at or under the app's build root (`${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}/menuz/build/macos`) and reads the list back. A record left there is a warning, and the exit stands. Xcode registers the build product, and that record can come back after the build's own drop, so the bundle id would resolve to a build product rather than the installed app (Utilz 0106).

## Fix

Defaults with overrides, so that a project whose app moves with it behaves exactly as today:

- **The app's version from its own source** (eg `macos.version_from`, defaulting to project.version_from and read by the same reader). The tag and the release stay the project's.
- **A freshness check that does not rest on the version:** a commit stamp the project names in the bundle's Info.plist, checked against the tag's commit wherever the version is checked now. When the app's version source differs from the project's and no stamp is declared, the built-in refuses rather than ship with no freshness proof. The design may settle this differently, under vc's review.
- **A declared kind stamp:** a key, and the value a release build must carry, checked beside the version.
- **macos.app naming a bundle outside the root without a machine-specific path:** a leading `~`, `$HOME` or `$XDG_*` is expanded, or a key's command prints the path.
- **The Launch Services drop on every path out** of every command that registers a copy. Signals are held through the drop and the removal, the record list is read back. A record left on the staged copy is a warning naming the command to clear it, and the exit stands: the next step drops it again, and Launch Services can register it again on its own (Utilz 0115). A record left on publish's proof copy, or its directory not removed, fails the run after a successful upload, leading with what is true, with no rerun suggested (utilz-vc, 2026-10-27; Utilz 0104 and 0106).
- **A last drop at the end of the release steps** for every record at or under the declared product's build root, read back. A record left there is a warning, and the exit stands. Or a declared hook that does the same, as the design settles.

## Done when

1. A project whose app takes its version from its own source signs, notarises and publishes under the project's tag. A project whose app carries the project's version behaves as before. A macos.bats arm holds each.
2. A bundle whose commit stamp is not a prefix of the tag's commit is refused at app-sign and at publish. With no tag in the tree, the stamp check refuses. With a separate version source and no declared stamp, the built-in refuses and names the key to declare, or does what the design settles.
3. A declared kind stamp with another value is refused wherever the version is checked.
4. A macos.app written with a leading `~`, `$HOME` or `$XDG_*` (or the chosen key) resolves to the bundle, and an unset variable is refused by name.
5. Each step that registers a copy drops its record on every path out, and a signal during the drop does not cut it short. A record left on the staged copy is a warning, naming the bundle and `lsregister -u <path>`, and the exit stands. A record left on publish's proof copy, or its directory not removed, fails the run after a successful upload, and the message leads with what is true ("published <asset> on release <tag>; could not drop ...").
6. After publish, no Launch Services record remains at or under the declared product's build root, read back, and a record left there is a warning that keeps the exit (or the declared hook does this).
7. lib/pages/macos.md and lib/config.reference.yaml document the new keys. The Resolution maps each check Utilz's command makes to the built-in's, and utilz-vc agrees that Utilz can delete its bin/.devbin/cmd/macos without losing any check it makes, Utilz 0115's included.
8. The landing suite passes under BSD and GNU (macos.bats, with the tree scans and help), and CI is green on the pushed head.

## Resolution

Fixed at b2fba596f14b1ec959cc26b424978cfd53af99ac, landed on main by vc with the rest of C (fb66b479..7565e2a2) on hv's GO of 29 Oct, as cc banked it. The built-in `macos` signs an app that versions apart from its project, checks its stamps against the tag, reads path keys from the home or an XDG directory, and drops every copy's Launch Services record on every path out, checked.

- **An app that versions apart.** `macos.version_from` names the file the app's own version is read from (default project.version_from). The app versions apart only when that file is not the project's version file, each placed by `version_path` (lib/helpers), the one rule read_version reads by (issue 0259), so an absolute project.version_from or macos.version_from naming the same file is not apart. The tag, the release and the attach stay the project's.
- **The stamps.** An app that versions apart must declare `macos.commit_stamp`, the Info.plist key its build writes its commit into, since its version cannot show a copy is the tag's build; the stamp must be 8 to 40 lowercase hex characters and a prefix of the tag's commit. `macos.kind_stamp`, with `macos.kind_value` (default release), checks the build's kind. Each is checked at app-sign on the staged copy, and at publish on the stapled copy and on the zip's own, with the tag in this tree (`tag_commit`, lib/cmd/macos's one read of the tag's commit); with the tag gone, `require_tag_head` refuses at app-sign and publish refuses before it uploads. The config refuses a kind_value without its kind_stamp, or an empty one, and macos validates the config at load.
- **Path keys.** A path key may open with `~`, `$HOME` or an XDG base-directory variable (`$XDG_STATE_HOME`, `$XDG_DATA_HOME`, `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME` or `$XDG_CACHE_HOME`, as `$X` or `${X}`), expanded by `path_expand` (lib/helpers) as `xdg_dir` reads it: an XDG variable counts only when absolute, and otherwise reads as its XDG default under an absolute HOME. Any other leading tilde or variable form (`~user`, `$FOO`, `${X:-...}`, `$HOMEX`), or a HOME that is not absolute below /, is refused, naming the key and what it opens with, so a value is never read as a path in the project. `xdg_dir` is the one statement of the XDG defaults, and 0272 reads infra's profile through it.
- **The drops, on every path out.** One EXIT trap, `drop_on_exit`, drops the staged copy, the Gatekeeper check's copy and publish's proof copy, with INT, TERM and HUP ignored through each drop and removal, and reads the record list back whole from `lsregister -dump`. A record left on the check or proof copy, which are gone, fails the run, saying first, after an upload, that the asset is published. One left on the staged copy warns, naming `lsregister -u <path>`, and the exit stands, since each step drops it again, publish the last. The Gatekeeper check runs in a dir of its own, dropped mid-command by `drop_check_copy`.
- **The last drop.** After the upload, publish drops every record at or under `macos.build_root` (default: the directory holding macos.app), deepest first (`ls_drop_under`), and one left warns, the exit standing, since a build can register its product again. It runs in a `$(...)` without the hold, so an interrupt during it exits 1 after publish has printed what it published. A root that is /, or holds the home directory, /Applications, ~/Applications, /System/Applications or /System/Library/CoreServices, is refused at app-sign and publish before anything is built or uploaded (`build_root_why`, `require_build_root`), and doctor reports it.
- **Placement.** `cargo_place` takes an optional getcwd, so macos places every path it compares with Launch Services as the filesystem spells it, publish's staging dir included.
- **doctor** names the lsregister every drop runs (`ls_cmd`) and the build root.

Documented in lib/pages/macos.md, lib/config.reference.yaml and docs/configuration.md. macos.bats's arms run against an lsregister fake that keeps its records in a file; whether a real `lsregister -u` on a removed bundle and a real `-dump` behave as the fake does is shown only on real hardware, and is confirmed at the first real publish, as are real signing and notarisation.

- **Done when 1.** "an app that versions apart signs, notarises and publishes under the project's tag and version, its commit stamp the tag's (0243)": an app at 0.4.7 in a project at 1.0.0 signs, notarises and publishes Demo.app.zip onto release v1.0.0. An app that carries the project's version behaves as before: macos.bats's arms from before 0243, "a staged copy with another bundle id, or another version, is refused and removed, with nothing signed" among them, run whole in the light phase; and the two arms critic-shell's R6 asked for, "macos.version_from naming the project's own version file, relatively, is not an app apart, so app-sign needs no commit stamp (0243)" and its twin at macos.bats:759, where macos.version_from and project.version_from both name the project's version file by an absolute path, hold that naming the project's own version file, either way, is not apart.
- **Done when 2.** "a commit stamp that is not the tag's commit, or not a commit, is refused at app-sign, and at publish (0243)" refuses a stamp of 16 hex characters that is no prefix of the tag's commit and one that is not hex, at app-sign with nothing signed, and at publish on the stapled copy with nothing uploaded. "with the tag gone from the tree, app-sign and publish refuse, naming it (0243)" holds the stamp check's refusal with no tag. This arm's red at the base comes through its setup, since the base cannot sign an app that versions apart. "an app that versions apart with no commit stamp declared is refused before anything is built, naming the key (0243)" refuses at app-sign and publish, naming macos.commit_stamp, before macos.build runs.
- **Done when 3.** "a declared kind stamp with another value is refused at app-sign, and at publish (0243)". "macos.kind_value without macos.kind_stamp, or empty, is refused as config, by doctor and by macos itself (0243)" holds the config's refusals.
- **Done when 4.** "macos.app written from the home or an XDG base directory resolves to a bundle outside the project, and any other leading tilde or variable form, or a HOME that is not absolute, is refused by name (0243)" resolves `~/`, `$HOME/` and `${HOME}/` to the home's bundle, and `${XDG_STATE_HOME}/` and `$XDG_STATE_HOME/` to XDG_STATE_HOME's bundle when it is absolute and to `~/.local/state`'s when it is relative or unset. The design settles the unset case by the XDG spec: an unset XDG variable reads as its default, not as a refusal. What is refused by name is any other variable or form (`$FOO`, `${XDG_STATE_HOME:-...}`, `~user`, `$HOMEX`) and a HOME that is not absolute, each naming macos.app and what it opens with. helpers.bats's "path_expand expands a leading tilde, HOME or XDG base-directory variable and nothing else, naming any other leading tilde or variable form, and xdg_dir reads each XDG variable, its own, only when it is absolute (0243)" holds path_expand and xdg_dir themselves, each XDG variable set distinct, set, relative and unset.
- **Done when 5.** "each step drops the record its tools gave the staged copy on its way out, a failed step and publish too, and a record that stays is a warning naming the command, the exit standing (0243)" holds app-sign's drop, app-notarize's warning naming `lsregister -u <path>` with exit 0, a failed app-notarize dropping a record Launch Services gave again, and publish's drop. "a record that stays on the Gatekeeper check's copy, which is gone, fails the step that made it, and the staged copy is dropped on the way out (0243)" and "a TERM during the Gatekeeper check ends the step, and its copy's record and its dir go on the way out (0243)" hold the check's copy, the TERM sent to the macos process itself, not a subshell. "a record that stays on publish's proof copy fails the run after the upload, saying first that the asset is published (0243)", "a proof dir that cannot be removed fails the run after the upload, saying first that the asset is published, and how to remove it (0243)" and "a record list that cannot be read after the upload fails the run, saying first that the asset is published (0243)" each exit 1 with the message leading "published Demo.app.zip on release v1.0.0; could not drop ...". "a TERM during the proof copy's drop does not cut it short: its record and its dir go, the list is read back, and publish exits 0 (0243)" holds the signal hold.
- **Done when 6.** "after the upload, publish drops every record under the build root, and one that stays is a warning, the exit standing (0243)" registers the build product as a real build can, and holds it dropped, then a record that stays warned with exit 0. "a build root that is /, or holds the home directory or a directory installed apps live in, is refused before anything is built or uploaded (0243)" holds each root build_root_why refuses, as typed, at app-sign and publish, with macos.build never run, and counts the rows it checked against its table's own count.
- **Done when 7.** lib/pages/macos.md, lib/config.reference.yaml and docs/configuration.md document macos.version_from, macos.commit_stamp, macos.kind_stamp, macos.kind_value, macos.build_root and the path keys' expansion. The map of Utilz's bin/.devbin/cmd/macos (U, unmoved on Utilz main since 14103179) has four homes, as utilz-vc gave them through vc on 2026-10-27, and Utilz deletes U only in its 0118, in the same change that adds the declared option and its build's check:
  1. **The built-in:** what it checked before 0243 and still checks: HEAD at the release tag in a clean tree, the staged copy outside the build tree with its bundle id and version, the signature inside-out with its identifier, team and hardened runtime read back, notarisation stapled only when Accepted, the Gatekeeper check, and publish's one upload through `release attach --from` with SHA256SUMS read back; and the rest of app-verify's dist mode.
  2. **0243's keys:** the app's version from its own source (macos.version_from); the commit stamp, 8 to 40 lowercase hex and a prefix of the tag's commit, on the staged copy and at publish on the stapled and zipped copies, refused with the tag absent (macos.commit_stamp); the kind stamp (macos.kind_stamp, macos.kind_value); the product outside the root (path_expand); the checked drops on every path out, signals held and the list read back, a staged copy's record a warning, a proof copy's record or dir a failure after the upload; and Utilz 0115's drop under the build root (macos.build_root).
  3. **Utilz's declared option:** app-icons (U:102-121), as `commands.macos.options.app-icons.run` with `in_all: false`, its script outside cmd/, and the doctor icon lines (U:125-150) as its own check. A declared option is routed before the handler and command tiers (lib/resolve), which 0243 does not touch.
  4. **Utilz's own build of the app:** app-verify's debug and release modes (U:586-613: the executable, LSUIElement true, the stamps), as a check on its own product after each build.
  Three of U's behaviours have no home of the four: store-creds' refusal of an empty value before storing (U:486-490), where the built-in hands entry to security(1)'s own prompt and whether that refuses an empty value is not established; the stamps each step prints on read-back (U:285-294, 313), a display rather than a check; and publish's interrupt exit codes 130, 143 and 129 (U:725-727), where the built-in exits 1. utilz-vc's reading of this map against U: AGREED. utilz-vc read this map against U (bin/.devbin/cmd/macos, unmoved on Utilz main since 14103179). U:102-121, 125-150 and 586-613 are the cited code, and every check U makes has a home. (a) The built-in refuses an empty notary credential at use, not before storing: load_creds reads each value back from the keychain, require_creds refuses any empty value before app-notarize (lib/cmd/macos:240-244 and 604 in the 0.1.15 vendored in Utilz), and doctor reports an empty one as MISSING. So no notarisation runs on an empty value, and the refusal moves from store-creds to its first use. (b) The stamps U prints on read-back (U:285-294, 313) are a display, and 0243's macos.commit_stamp and macos.kind_stamp/kind_value check them on each copy, which covers what the display showed. (c) Publish's interrupt exiting 1, not 130, 143 or 129 (U:725-727), is a change hv accepted on 27 Oct (Utilz vc decision 68, item 3). Utilz deletes U only in its 0118, on the 0.1.16 it vendors.
- **Done when 8.** The landing suite: C's arms phase, in estate slot 01M61TNPWJTZMYNDBPTEZZ54ZG on molt-vc's grant, ran every arm tagged with one of the bank's eight issues on main 09c7d61a, file by file, from 2026-10-28 18:00Z to 18:08Z: in the red clone f4b30a50, main's lib with the bank's tests, under BSD; then at the bank's tip 53c92332 under BSD, and again with GNU coreutils, findutils, sed and grep first on PATH (~/Devel/scratch/devbin-cc/s5e/runs/arms/, summary in s5e/arms.out). Of 0243's 19 arms, 17 failed in the red clone, and the two holding that a version_from naming the project's own version file is not an app apart passed there, as they should on main. Under BSD and GNU 18 passed, and the Done when 4 arm failed on its expected message, shorter than the refusal the lib prints. C was stopped on hv's word in its light phase, so its whole-file legs, the tree scans among them, did not finish; hv's runs on main took them over. hv's first test all on main (tmp/test/20261029-0614) found four failures in 0243's code and test, which caf77878 fixed: contract.bats 338, where ls_records now returns 1 where the list cannot be read; helpers.bats 1204 (0082), where path_expand now reads the variable's name by parameter expansion and asks is_identifier, so the charset is spelled only there; neutral.bats 1719 (0152), where build_root_why now holds HOME in a local; and macos.bats 1707, the Done when 4 arm, which now expects the refusal's full wording, the lib's message unchanged. hv's `dvb test all` on rhadamanth at 217adf65 ran every one of the 2777 tests bats counts in tests/unit once, and none failed (tmp/test/20261029-0817.bats.out, its .errors empty). K0116B, the full suite on kovacs at 4d1a76b0 with rustup's cargo first on PATH, as on CI's Ubuntu runner, is green, as vc read its seal. CI run 40851772728 on 4d1a76b0 and CI run 40860048152 on 25175386, the head 0.1.16 was cut from, are green on Test on Ubuntu, Shell Script Analysis and Test Summary. No critic leg ran on the landed commits.

- **CI:** run 40860048152 on the pushed head 25175386, which carries the landing, read green by vc.
